rationale: All four units must be committed to satisfy N-1 security. Any 3-unit subset fails the constraint: after losing g3 (largest at 180MW), remaining capacity must exceed 300MW. Only with all units committed do we have 550MW total capacity, leaving 370MW after N-1 loss—sufficient to cover the 300MW requirement (260MW demand + 40MW reserve). Total commitment cost is startup costs (400+550+700+220=$1870) plus no-load costs (80+100+120+60=$360).
